blocks.text: By accessing the Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For Zscaler-hosted and Outpost (hybrid) deployments of DSPM, logs include:

blocks.item: Cloud Service Provider (CSP) activity audit logs

blocks.text: In addition, subject to your configuration and enablement, the following logs are also processed:

blocks.item: Data residing in cloud data stores such as databases, storage services, and data volumes (disks) is scanned and classified. Raw data is not saved, only metadata is stored and reported.
Data systems are scanned for security vulnerabilities, and information about any discovered security vulnerabilities is stored.

blocks.text: All logs that describe active cloud resources or issues are retained by Zscaler for the duration of the subscription. Once the resources are no longer present in the CSP, DSPM maintains the logs for a rolling period of 180 days during the term of the subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, Zscaler deletes the logs after the 180-day retention cycle or earlier upon request.
For customer-hosted deployments of DSPM, Zscaler does not process or store any data.
During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.
If you choose to enable the storage of evidence samples, logs will also include raw data samples.
